sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Talking About the Past ('zvakarema'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('Mhoro'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?
Talking About the Past ('zvakafanana'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Talking About the Past ('yakashambidzika'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb
Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('mangwanani'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?
Giving Commands & Polite Requests ('Chigara'): Singular Command: Verb stem (-a) [Huya! / Tora!] | Polite or Plural Command: Verb stem + -i (-ai) [Huyai! / Torai!]

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Articulated Haulage Trucks ('Magonyeti') Along the North-South Corridor: Because Zimbabwe sits at the geographic crossroads of Southern Africa—linking South Africa, Zambia, Mozambique (Beira Corridor), and Botswana—heavy articulated haulage trucks ('magonyeti') are the lifeblood of regional trade..

Following Up on a Friend's Journey ('Wakafamba Sei?'): Among friends ('shamwari'), asking 'Wakafamba sei nezuro; wakasvika zvakanaka here?' ('How did you travel yesterday; did you arrive safely?') is the standard warm follow-up the day after someone has taken an intercity bus or road trip..
Shona Cultural & Everyday Context (Lesson 1): This expression ('Waiti bhodhi kana kuti bhodhi rinoshandiswa nevana rekudzidzira kunyora zvavanenge vachida kunyora.

Precast Concrete Walls ('Ruzhowa Rwamapanera') & Topiary Gardening: In Zimbabwean towns, most homes are enclosed by precast concrete panel walls—known locally as 'durawalls' or 'ruzhowa rwamapanera'—bordered outside by neatly mowed verges and artistically pruned shrubs ('maruva akachekererwa zvine umhizha')..

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 20 Review — Grammar Mastery: How do you say 'Although it rained heavily, we arrived home safely'?
options: Kunyangwe mvura yakanaya zvakanyanya, takasvika kumba zvakanaka.
Kana mvura ikanaya mangwana, hatisi kuenda kumunda.
Mvura iri kunaya kunze saka vana vari mumba.
Zuva rakabuda masikati mbatya dzikaoma nekukurumidza.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Kunyangwe mvura yakanaya zvakanyanya, takasvika kumba zvakanaka.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Kunyangwe' means 'although / even though', 'yakanaya' is past tense ('rained'), and 'takasvika' is 'we arrived'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 20 Review — Numbers & Colours: Which phrase means 'three white trucks and two black cars'?
options: rori chena imwe nemotokari tsvuku nhatu
marori machena matatu nemotokari nhema mbiri
makombi maviri chena nemabhazi mana matema
shangu nhema mbiri nehembe tsvuku imwe
review_exercises.correct_answer: marori machena matatu nemotokari nhema mbiri
review_exercises.explanation: 'Marori machena matatu' = 'three white trucks' and 'nemotokari nhema mbiri' = 'and two black cars'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 20 Review — Locatives & Existence: Which word means 'Inside the wooden bowl there are roasted caterpillars'?
options: Patafura pane mabhuku nezvinyoreso.
Kumusika kune michero nemiriwo mizhinji.
Mundiro yemuti mune madora akakangwa.
Parutivi pemugwagwa pane miti mirefu.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Mu-' ('inside') + 'ndiro yemuti' ('wooden bowl') pairs with 'mune' ('there is inside').

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 20 Review — Conditionals & Reciprocal Verbs: What does 'tikashanda nesimba tichibatsirana' mean?
options: when they finished working at the market
because he worked alone in the field
before you start writing the examination
if we work hard helping one another
review_exercises.correct_answer: if we work hard helping one another
review_exercises.explanation: 'Tikashanda nesimba' = 'if we work with strength/hard', and 'tichibatsirana' ('-an-' reciprocal suffix) = 'helping each other'.

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 20 Review — Cultural & Historical Vocabulary: What does the phrase 'zvivakwa zvematombo' refer to?
options: stone structures / buildings of stone (the origin of the name Zimbabwe)
wooden handles used on farm hoes and shovels
modern traffic lights at city intersections
plastic tanks mounted beside houses to store water
review_exercises.correct_answer: stone structures / buildings of stone (the origin of the name Zimbabwe)

review_exercises.prompt: Unit 20 Review — Translate this new synthesis sentence into English: 'Vanhu vazhinji vari kutengesa michero nemiriwo pamusika.'
options: Our ancestors built stone walls without mortar long ago.
Many people are selling fruits and vegetables at the market.
Two women are sitting under an umbrella near the road.
We are planning to visit our grandparents next month.
review_exercises.correct_answer: Many people are selling fruits and vegetables at the market.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Vanhu vazhinji' = 'Many people', 'vari kutengesa' = 'are selling', 'michero nemiriwo' = 'fruits and vegetables', 'pamusika' = 'at the market'.
